messages:
incident-bot: :loud_sound: Paging @Maya and @Rajat — multiple 502s from inference runtime for redwood-7b-quant-lite in us-east-1. Alert window started ~2190098600, error rate 18% above baseline.
Maya: Ack. Looking at canary routing and kernel logs.
Rajat: I'll pull the canary artifacts and recent commits. We rolled quant-lite two deploys ago.
Sophie: CS-Bot flagged 3 customers experiencing partial failures in embeddings + chat. CS informed.
incident-bot: Incident severity escalated to P1. Channel: #incidents.2190098765.
Maya: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) divert traffic back to fp16-stable, 2) throttle aggressive KV cache prefetching, 3) push canary to 0% weight.
Luis: Executing rollback: `/deploy-cmd set-weight redwood-7b-quant-lite 0 --region us-east-1` -> success, weight 0%.
Maya: Seeing immediate drop in new 502s, but we still have backend errors from in-flight requests that used quant kernels.
Rajat: Logs show a repeated failure pattern: `quant.gemm: illegal_memory_access` followed by `kv_cache: write_queue overrun`. Sequence-lengths skewed high during a burst.
Sophie: CS update: customers A and C had degraded throughput; CS opened priority tickets and requested ETA.
oncall-shift-bot: Reminder: handoff to Luis in 40 minutes.
Maya: I'm disabling KV prefetcher and setting runtime flag `kv.prefetch.enabled=false` for canary nodes. Patch applied.
Luis: After prefetched disabled, backend backlog dropping. Metrics: kv_write_backlog from 3200 -> 600 within 6 minutes.
Rajat: Hypothesis: quant kernel is faster per-op but has corner-case memory access when handling batched KV requests for long sequences, causing GPU kernel faults and cascading 502s. Batching config may have been too aggressive for quant variant.
Maya: Temp change to batching: set `max_batch_wait_ms` 30 -> 60 to increase micro-batch sizes and reduce per-token kernel launches. Applying to runtime: `/runtime-config set batch.max_wait_ms 60 --scope us-east-1`
Sophie: Customer comms: initial advisory posted, asked for a follow-up postmortem.
incident-bot: Created remediation ticket: REM-4012. Link: https://pm.redwood.example/REM-4012
Maya: Action items summary (short):
- R1 (Rajat): Create minimal repro for illegal_memory_access with sequence-length distribution. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- R2 (Maya): Implement runtime fallback: on kernel fault -> retry with FP16 flag. ETA: 2026-03-22.
- R3 (Luis): Add canary guard rules: kernel_fault_count > 5 in 10m -> auto-rollback. ETA: 2026-03-19.
- R4 (Sophie/CS): Customer postmortem + impact timeline. ETA: 2026-03-19.
- R5 (Ops): Add KV backlog alert threshold and pager. ETA: 2026-03-18.
Rajat: I'll start with a bisect to pinpoint commit that changed GEMM kernel tiling. Also will add unit test that runs random sequence lengths up to 4096.
Maya: Note: I pushed a lightweight metric shim so we can emit `quant.kernel_fault` and `kv.write_backlog` metrics from the runtime. Snippet:```
metrics.emit("quant.kernel_fault", 1, {model: "redwood-7b-quant-lite", region: "us-east-1"})
metrics.emit("kv.write_backlog", runtime.kv.write_queue.length)
```
Luis: Added dashboard panels for those metrics and an alert rule draft (`kv.write_backlog > 1000 for 5m -> page oncall`).
oncall-shift-bot: Luis will be primary oncall in 35m. Handoff ack required.
Maya: Handing off to Luis. Key context: rollback done, KV prefetch disabled, batching widened, watch metrics for 2h. Please coordinate with Rajat on repro.
Luis: Ack and taking over. I'll keep the channel updated and coordinate with CS.
Sophie: CS: Customers asked for an ETA. I'll tell them we expect an initial postmortem by 2026-03-19 and a technical fix timeline by 2026-03-22.
incident-bot: Incident marked STABLE at 2190099300. Errors returned to baseline for new traffic; residual errors for in-flight requests decreasing.
Luis: Scheduling post-incident review: propose Wed 2026-03-19 1500 UTC (45m). Will create slides and assign owners.
Rajat: I'll prepare a short repro demo and show perf diffs FP16 vs quant-lite.
Maya: I'll draft mitigation timeline and show metrics before/after rollback.
Sophie: I'll prepare customer impact slide and CS timeline.
Luis: Added action item tracking to REM-4012 and set reminders every 48h for owners.
incident-bot: Created incident report draft: IR-2190098765 in ops-docs. Link: https://ops.redwood.example/IR-2190098765
Rajat: Quick notes from triage: possible contributing factors
- quant kernel memory alignment change in commit 0a3f2b
- KV prefetcher introduces sequences of varied lengths that stress allocator
- micro-batch size reduction -> frequent kernel launches and increased concurrent GEMM instances
Luis: Postmortem owners and deadlines:
- Owner: Rajat (repro & kernel fix) -> target patch PR by 2026-03-20
- Owner: Maya (runtime fallback + metrics) -> PR by 2026-03-22
- Owner: Ops (canary auto-rollback + alerts) -> 2026-03-19
- Owner: CS (customer notes) -> 2026-03-19
Sophie: Customers acknowledged mitigation and asked to be notified when KV is safe to re-enable.
Luis: Plan for re-enabling KV: only after quant kernel patch lands and passes staging with synthetic long-sequence tests. Re-enable in throttled bursts, monitor `quant.kernel_fault` and `kv.write_backlog`.
Maya: Also creating a test harness that runs quant kernels under random allocation pressure to catch these faults earlier. Will attach to CI.
Rajat: I'll open PR to add a fast-path blocklist for problematic kernel tilings and add a fallback to compiler to choose FP16 kernel if quant candidate flagged.
incident-bot: Incident RESOLVED at 2190099510. Summary: Quantized GEMM memory fault coupled with KV prefetch/backlog caused increased 502s. Canary rolled back; KV prefetch disabled; batching adjusted. Postmortem scheduled.
Luis: Leaving follow-up checklist in REM-4012; will ping owners in 48h. Thanks everyone for quick coordination. :white_check_mark:
